statement: Let V = {0,...,n-1}. Let E be the set of unordered pairs {edges[i][0], edges[i][1]} for 0 <= i < len(edges). Let S = sum_{v in V} values[v]. For a subset R of E, let G_R be the graph with vertex set V and edge set E \ R; its connected components partition V. Call R valid if for every connected component C of G_R, the integer sum_{v in C} values[v] is divisible by k. If S is not divisible by k, set r = 0; otherwise set r = max { |R| + 1 | R is a valid subset of E }. The function returns Result.ok r, where r is the i64 representing this integer.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 30000; len(edges) = n - 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(edges), len(edges[i]) = 2 and 0 <= edges[i][0], edges[i][1] < n; edges represents a valid undirected tree on nodes 0,...,n-1; len(values) = n; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= values[i] <= 10^9; 1 <= k <= 10^9; all sums mentioned in the statement are within the i64 range.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result: there exists an i64 r such that max_k_divisible_components n edges values k = Result.ok r. It does not fail by overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.

statement: Let V = {0,...,n-1} and E = {{edges[i][0], edges[i][1]} | 0 <= i < len(edges)}. For each e in E, deleting e from the tree splits V into two connected components; define T as the set of e in E for which at least one of these two components has value divisible by k. Then the function returns Result.ok r with r = |T| + 1.
